question_text:
A structural design involves a steel wire 2 mm in diameter that will carry an electrical current. If the resistance of the wire must be less than $25 \Omega$, calculate the maximum length of the wire, given the data in Table. Give your answer as the value of maximum_length.
(Table:
\begin{tabular}{llc}
\hline Electrical Conductivities of Some Materials at Room Temperature \\
\hline Conducting range & Material & Conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}\left(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{\mathbf{- 1}} \cdot \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{- 1}} \mathbf{)}\right.$ \\
\hline Conductors & Aluminum (annealed) & $35.36 \times 10^6$ \\
& Copper (annealed standard) & $58.00 \times 10^6$ \\
& Iron (99.99 + \%) & $10.30 \times 10^6$ \\
Semiconductors & Steel (wire) & $5.71-9.35 \times 10^6$ \\
& Germanium (high purity) & 2.0 \\
& Silicon (high purity) & $0.40 \times 10^{-3}$ \\
Insulators & Lead sulfide (high purity) & 38.4 \\
& Aluminum oxide & $10^{-10}-10^{-12}$ \\
& Borosilicate glass & $10^{-13}$ \\
& Polyethylene & $10^{-13}-10^{-15}$ \\
& Nylon 66 & $10^{-12}-10^{-13}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
)The unit of the answer is m.
response:
## Solution

The resistance of a wire is given by:

$$R = \frac{L}{\sigma A}$$

where:
- $L$ = length of the wire
- $\sigma$ = electrical conductivity
- $A$ = cross-sectional area

**Given data:**
- Diameter $d = 2\text{ mm} \Rightarrow r = 1\times10^{-3}\text{ m}$
- Cross-sectional area: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi(1\times10^{-3})^2 = \pi\times10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$
- Steel (wire) conductivity: $\sigma = 5.71\text{–}9.35 \times 10^{6}\ \Omega^{-1}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}$
- Resistance constraint: $R < 25\ \Omega$

**Finding maximum length:**

$$L = R\,\sigma\,A$$

To obtain the *maximum* length, we use the **maximum** conductivity value, $\sigma = 9.35\times10^{6}\ \Omega^{-1}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}$, and the resistance limit $R = 25\ \Omega$:

$$L_{\max} = (25)(9.35\times10^{6})(\pi\times10^{-6})$$

$$L_{\max} = 25 \times 9.35 \times \pi = 734.35\text{ m}$$

$$\boxed{734.35}$$
